newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Harbour told to recruit calibre props.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Harbour told to recruit calibre props.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Oct 14 - Everyone concerned knew it, but no-one dared saying it publicly until North Harbour rugby coach Brad Meurant did on Saturday.
His team has to find more suitable props if they are to be competitive in next year's national provincial championship (NPC), he said.
Harbour were thrashed 69-27 on Saturday by a rampant Auckland team riding high on their enormous All Blacks experience.

It was Harbour's third Ranfurly Shield Challenge loss to as many teams this season. They won only two of their eight championship matches despite boasting current All Blacks Ian Jones, Frank Bunce, Walter Little, Eric Rush and Glen Osborne in their lineup.

The problem for North Harbour was evident again in the first scrum against Auckland when tighthead prop Gavin Walsh was outdone by All Blacks's loosehead Craig Dowd. The game, Meurant said later, was well and truly over right there and then.
"I think we've got to look at our front row -- that is realistic," Meurant told NZPA after the 10-tries-to-three hiding.
"The guys out there did their best, but the reality is if you can't scrum then you don't win games.
"Our pack hadn't competed all year and that is an area that has to be picked up on."
He said Harbour's backs looked tired and had played a lot of football this year but so had Auckland's. The major difference was that the forwards hadn't gone as well as Auckland's had.
"When you're not going well that tends to manifest itself."
Auckland led 31-13 at the break scoring five tries. They added another five in the second half.
Although Harbour tried gamely to go the distance with them, they lost the pace and intensity of Auckland, who largely resembled an All Blacks' juggernaut.
Meurant said North Harbour should actively recruit high calibre props in this professional era and his captain Richard Turner agreed.
"In the past we've been able to get by, but when it comes to occasions like this and shield challenges we've always struggled because we don't have parity upfront," Turner said.
"I know it's a cliche but if you haven't got it then it makes for a pretty long day. Obviously it is where the game starts and if you're on the backfoot from the beginning it makes it difficult."
Turner said Harbour couldn't liberate their Rolls Royce backline which boasts the likes of Little, Bunce, Rush, Peter Woods and Osborne because their ball security up front couldn't be guaranteed.
Auckland's dominance upfront was emphasised by the fact that their backs ran freely all afternoon and produced a hat-tricks of tries to wingers James Kerr and Brian Lima.
Auckland play Otago next Saturday in one NPC semifinal at Eden Park while Counties take on Canterbury at Pukekohe Stadium on Sunday in the other semifinal.
